title: ALMA Measurements of the HNC and HC<SUB>3</SUB>N Distributions in Titan's Atmosphere
question: What are the spatial distributions and vertical abundance profiles of HNC and HC3N in Titan's atmosphere as seen by ALMA?

what.value: Titan temperature profile from Cassini CIRS and HASI

evidence.quote: The atmospheric temperature profile was generated from a combination of Cassini CIRS and HASI measurements

what.value: Line parameters and partition functions from JPL catalog; frequencies from Okabayashi & Tanimoto (HNC), Thorwirth et al. (HC3N)

evidence.quote: Spectral line parameters and partition functions were taken from the JPL catalog

recipe.method: Standard ALMA calibration, flux scaling to Titan model, continuum subtraction, Hogbom cleaning

recipe.goal: Make integrated emission maps in Titan frame
recipe.method: Transform to projected distances and Titan rest frame; integrate ±1 km/s (HNC), ±5 km/s (HC3N)
Integrate cubes over 1.5'' diameter circular aperture centered on Titan
NEMESIS line-by-line radiative transfer with two-parameter gradient model (abundance at z_r=293 km, slope as fraction of scale height); HNC step model above 400 km
key_parameters: 10-point trapezium-rule integration to model top at 782 km
assumptions: Profiles do not vary with latitude/longitude; HC3N condenses below ~71 km; Lorentz half-widths 1.290 (HNC), 0.1 (HC3N) cm-1/bar, exponents 0.69, 0.75

recipe.goal: Map HC3N line core vs wings
recipe.method: Integrate core (-0.5 to 0.5 km/s) and wings (2.0-5.0 km/s) separately to probe altitude

evidence.quote: The best-fitting abundance above 400 km was found to be $4.85\pm0.28$ ppb
are offset clockwise by $40\pm5^{\circ}$ in the plane of the sky

not_stated_but_needed: Exact CASA task parameters and clean mask
Temperature/aerosol profile files used in NEMESIS
Aperture centering details and HC3N/HNC profile grids
score_reason: Imaging is described but the radiative-transfer inputs and scripts are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, imaging parameters are largely given, and results are numeric, though the NEMESIS modeling needs unstated inputs.
